We are on a mission to provide the highest quality service possible and bridging the digital divide across the globe. We work across a variety of different industries and one of the first global leaders in our space that is constantly innovating and working with the latest technologies. Position Overview We are seeking a Senior Hardware Engineer to lead the design, development, and validation of high-performance electronic products with an emphasis on RF systems and PCB design. The role will drive hardware architecture from concept through production, solving complex mixed-signal and high-speed challenges while collaborating with cross-functional teams (firmware, mechanical, systems) and mentoring junior engineers. The successful candidate will be hands-on in schematic capture, PCB layout reviews, lab validation and failure analysis to ensure reliable, manufacturable products. Key Responsibilities Lead end-to-end hardware development including requirements capture, architecture, schematic design, PCB layout coordination, and design for manufacturability focused on RF and mixed-signal systems. Design, simulate, and validate RF front-ends, analog and digital circuits including filters, mixers, amplifiers, and oscillators; optimize for noise, linearity, and signal integrity. Create and review PCB layouts for high-speed and mixed-signal designs, enforce stackup, routing, and grounding best practices, and work with PCB fabricators and assembly partners. Develop and execute test plans, perform bench validation and characterization using oscilloscopes, VNAs, spectrum analyzers, and other lab equipment; capture and analyze measurement data to drive design improvements. Debug prototypes and production units, perform root-cause analysis, implement corrective actions, and support yield and reliability improvements. Work closely with firmware and FPGA engineers to define interfaces (Ethernet, serial communication, high-speed serializers/deserializers) and support integration and bring-up activities. Drive design reviews, document design decisions, produce datasheets/BOMs, and maintain thorough design documentation to meet regulatory and quality requirements. Mentor and coach junior engineers, provide technical leadership across projects, and collaborate with program managers to meet schedules and deliverables. review_candidates.description: Location: Anywhere in Country At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence. We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world. Role Snapshot Client-facing Life Sciences manufacturing professional who helps design, build, test, and deploy digital solutions for regulated plant operations. The role combines practical knowledge of manufacturing processes with hands-on skills in manufacturing systems, industrial data, integration, analytics, and AI-enabled workflows. The Opportunity As a Senior in Supply Chain Manufacturing, you will work with pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical-device clients to connect production, quality, laboratory, engineering, and supply chain needs with deployable technology. You will contribute across the delivery lifecycle, from plant and system assessments through requirements, solution design, configuration support, testing, deployment, adoption, and stabilization. You will work directly with operators, engineers, quality teams, IT and OT specialists, data teams, and technology providers. You will own assigned technical and functional deliverables, help resolve implementation issues, and make clear recommendations to your workstream lead. The role calls for someone who can examine a shop-floor workflow, trace the data and systems behind it, and turn what they learn into a design or testable requirement. Your Key Responsibilities In this role, you will: Assess manufacturing and quality workflows, user needs, system interfaces, equipment data, and current-state pain points through site observations, interviews, workshops, and data review. Document process flows, user stories, functional requirements, data mappings, interface requirements, controls, and acceptance criteria for digital manufacturing solutions. Support the design and implementation of capabilities such as manufacturing execution, electronic batch records and electronic device history records (eDHRs), recipe and routing management, batch and unit genealogy, review by exception, connected-worker workflows, and plant performance reporting. Trace information across relevant systems, including MES/MOM, ERP, LIMS, QMS, historians, SCADA, DCS/PLC, and asset-management platforms; identify data gaps, inconsistent definitions, and integration dependencies. Develop and review equipment and batch hierarchies, source-to-target mappings, data-quality rules, and contextualized datasets with manufacturing, automation, and data specialists. Work with solution architects and engineers on interface specifications, APIs, industrial connectivity, and the movement of data between plant, edge, and enterprise environments. Configure or prototype solution components where appropriate to your experience and the engagement, and document design decisions for review by technical and client leads. Prepare and execute functional and integration test scripts, record defects, support resolution and retesting, and maintain traceability between requirements and test evidence. Support deployment readiness, cutover, user training, hypercare, and handover by preparing clear technical documentation and responding to issues from plant users. Partner with client quality and validation teams to prepare or review applicable documentation concerning GxP, data integrity, electronic records, change control, and computer system validation or risk-based assurance. Contribute to analytics and AI use cases by assessing source-data quality, defining manufacturing context, checking outputs against operational workflows, and documenting where human review is needed. Communicate progress, risks, dependencies, and recommended next steps to client counterparts and engagement leaders; coordinate defined tasks with junior colleagues when needed. Skills And Attributes For Success To thrive in this role, you should be able to work in depth in at least one technical area while collaborating across the broader manufacturing solution. You will bring: Manufacturing and quality understanding: Knowledge of how production execution, batch records, equipment, materials, laboratory results, deviations, and quality review connect in a regulated plant. Manufacturing technology skills: Hands-on functional, configuration, integration, testing, or support experience with one or more manufacturing, quality, laboratory, automation, or industrial-data solutions. Data and integration skills: Ability to identify source systems, interpret batch and equipment data, document mappings and interfaces, investigate data-quality issues, and explain how information moves between OT and enterprise systems. Delivery discipline: Ability to produce accurate requirements, design documents, test scripts, defect records, and deployment materials, and to follow issues through resolution. Technical communication: Ability to discuss an operational problem with a plant user and document it clearly enough for a developer, data engineer, automation specialist, or tester to act on. Regulated-delivery awareness: Understanding of why documentation, traceability, controlled changes, and reliable data matter when a solution supports GxP activities. Analytical judgment: Curiosity about AI and advanced analytics, paired with the ability to test whether the underlying data, workflow, and proposed output are fit for use. To qualify for the role, you must have: A bachelor’s degree in engineering, life sciences, manufacturing, information systems, computer science, supply chain, or a related discipline. At least 3 years of relevant experience in Life Sciences manufacturing, manufacturing systems, automation, industrial data, systems implementation, technology consulting, or a related field. Experience working with manufacturing or quality processes in a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical-device, or comparably regulated environment. Experience producing technical or functional delivery artifacts, such as requirements, process maps, data mappings, interface specifications, configuration documents, test scripts, or deployment materials. Experience collaborating with both operational stakeholders and technical delivery teams to investigate requirements, resolve issues, or implement a solution. Ability to travel as needed based on business and role requirements. Travel can range from 80-100%. Ideally, you’ll also have: Experience with MES/MOM, electronic batch records or eDHRs, recipe management, LIMS, QMS, historians, SCADA, DCS/PLC, connected-worker solutions, or industrial data platforms. Experience examining manufacturing data from more than one source and relating it to assets, materials, products, orders, recipes, batches, or quality events. Familiarity with ISA-88/IEC 61512 batch concepts, ISA-95/IEC 62264 manufacturing information models, or industrial connectivity approaches such as OPC UA and MQTT/Sparkplug. Exposure to GxP computer system validation, risk-based software assurance, data-integrity controls, electronic records, or OT cybersecurity considerations relevant to the system being delivered. Familiarity with Process Analytical Technology (PAT) and continuous improvement practices, including the use of manufacturing data to monitor process performance, identify variability, and improve quality, throughput, and operational performance. Experience supporting analytics or AI use cases in manufacturing or quality, such as process monitoring, predictive maintenance, deviation investigation, or decision support. Experience with drug substance, drug product, biologics, sterile manufacturing, medical devices, or technology transfer. Relevant platform, cloud, data, automation, Agile, or manufacturing certification. What We Look For We are looking for a Senior who enjoys getting close to the manufacturing process and the technology that supports it. The strongest candidates ask precise questions, produce dependable technical work, recognize when data or design assumptions do not hold up, and collaborate well with plant, quality, and technology teams to make solutions usable in practice. Learn more at ey.com/us/careers.
